stimuli.title: Eight persons (Aarav, Bhavna, etc.) live in a four-storey building. The bottom floor is 1 and the top floor is 4. Each floor has two flats: Flat A and Flat B. Flat A is to the west of Flat B.
stimuli.body:
Study the following information carefully:
• Zara lives on an odd numbered floor in Flat B.
• Meera lives immediately above Manish in the same flat.
• Rohan lives to the west of Deepak on floor 1.
• There is exactly one floor between the floors on which Zara and Rohan live.
• Meera lives on Floor 3 in Flat A.

(Note: One flat on each floor is Flat A and the other is Flat B).
stimuli.solution: Floor 4: Flat A = Zoya, Flat B = Esha | Floor 3: Flat A = Meera, Flat B = Zara | Floor 2: Flat A = Manish, Flat B = Tanvi | Floor 1: Flat A = Rohan, Flat B = Deepak

stimuli.title: Eight persons sitting around a circular table facing inside and outside
stimuli.body:
• Eight persons Wami, Gauri, Uday, Farhan and Vikas, Tanvi, Ojas, Yogesh sit around a circular table.
• Four of them face the center and four face away from the center (outside).
• Uday faces the center and sits second to the left of Gauri.
• Ojas sits immediately to the right of Uday.
• There are two persons sitting between Yogesh and Tanvi.
• Farhan faces Center and sits opposite to Uday.
• Vikas sits third to the right of Ojas.
stimuli.solution: Uday (Seat 1, facing Center), Ojas (Seat 2, facing Outside), Gauri (Seat 3, facing Center), Yogesh (Seat 4, facing Outside), Farhan (Seat 5, facing Center), Vikas (Seat 6, facing Outside), Tanvi (Seat 7, facing Center), Wami (Seat 8, facing Outside)

stimuli.title: Eight persons attending exam on 7th and 21st of March, April, May, and June
stimuli.body:
• Eight persons have their exams on two different dates (7th and 21st) across four consecutive months (March, April, May, June).
• Kunal attends the exam on 21st of a month having 30 days.
• Only two persons attend the exam between Kunal and Sneha.
• Yash attends the exam immediately before Varun.
• The number of persons attending before Ananya is the same as the number of persons attending after Esha.
• Tanvi attends on an odd date in a month having 31 days.
stimuli.solution: March 7: Kunal; March 21: Sneha; April 7: Yash; April 21: Varun; May 7: Ananya; May 21: Esha; June 7: Tanvi; June 21: Zoya

stimuli.title: Ten persons in two parallel rows facing North and South
stimuli.body:
• Ten persons sit in two parallel rows containing five persons each, such that there is equal distance between adjacent persons.
• In Row 1: A, B, C, D, and E sit and all of them face South.
• In Row 2: P, Q, R, S, and T sit and all of them face North.
• S sits at one of the extreme ends of Row 2.
• The one who faces S sits opposite to D.
• C sits second to the left of D.
• P sits opposite to B.
• Only two persons sit between Q and T.
stimuli.solution: Row 1 (South): D - C - B - E - A | Row 2 (North): S - Q - P - R - T

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few laptops are tablets. All tablets are computers. No computer is a mobile.
Conclusions: I. Some laptops are not tablets. II. No tablet is a mobile.
Which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements?
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few laptops are tablets' means Some laptops are tablets AND Some laptops are NOT tablets. Hence I follows.
2. Since All tablets are within computers and No computer is a mobile, tablets and mobiles are disjoint. Hence II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few banks are offices. Few offices are cabins. All cabins are rooms.
Conclusions: I. All banks being offices is a possibility. II. Some offices are rooms.
Which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements?
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few banks are offices' strictly forbids All banks from being offices. Thus I is NOT a possibility.
2. Since Few offices are cabins and All cabins are rooms, the intersection of offices and cabins must be rooms. Hence II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some circles are squares. No square is a triangle. All triangles are rectangles.
Conclusions: I. Some circles can never be triangles. II. All squares being rectangles is a possibility.
Which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. The common part of circles that are squares cannot enter triangles (since No square is triangle). Hence Some circles can never be triangles follows.
2. Squares and rectangles have no direct negative restriction, so all squares inside rectangles is a valid possibility. Hence II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few pens are pencils. No pencil is an eraser. Some erasers are scales.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are not erasers. II. All erasers being pens is a possibility.
Which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. Pens that are pencils cannot be erasers, so Some pens are not erasers follows.
2. Erasers have no direct negative relation with pens, so All erasers can overlap pens as a possibility. Hence both follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few books are papers. Some papers are notes. All notes are diaries.
Conclusions: I. All books are diaries. II. No paper is a diary.
Which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. No direct universal inclusion connects books and diaries. Hence I does not follow.
2. In fact, Some papers are notes and All notes are diaries means Some papers ARE diaries, contradicting II. Hence neither follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: P > Q ≥ R = S; T ≤ U < R; W ≥ P
Conclusions: I. W > S  II. P > T
Which of the conclusions is definitely true?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
From statements: W ≥ P > Q ≥ R = S ⇒ W > S (Conclusion I follows).
Also P > R and R > U ≥ T ⇒ P > T (Conclusion II follows).

questions.stem:
Statements: A ≥ B > C = D; E < F ≤ C; G > B
Conclusions: I. G > E  II. A ≥ F
Which of the conclusions is definitely true?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
From statements: G > B > C > F > E ⇒ G > E (Conclusion I follows).
Comparing A and F: A ≥ B > C ≥ F ⇒ A > F, not A ≥ F. Hence II does not follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: K ≤ L < M = N; O ≥ P > L; Q ≤ K
Conclusions: I. O > K  II. N > Q
Which of the conclusions is definitely true?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
From statements: O ≥ P > L ≥ K ⇒ O > K (Conclusion I follows).
Also N = M > L ≥ K ≥ Q ⇒ N > Q (Conclusion II follows).

questions.stem:
Statements: H > I ≥ J < K; L ≤ M < I; N ≥ J
Conclusions: I. H > M  II. K > N
Which of the conclusions is definitely true?
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
Comparing H and M: H > I and M < I, so both H and M are related to I in opposite directions (cannot establish definite relationship). Conclusion I does not follow.
Comparing K and N: J < K and N ≥ J gives opposite signs between K and N. Hence neither follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: V ≥ W > X = Y; Z ≤ Y; U < V
Conclusions: I. W > Z  II. V > X
Which of the conclusions is definitely true?
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
From statements: W > X = Y ≥ Z ⇒ W > Z (Conclusion I follows).
Also V ≥ W > X ⇒ V > X (Conclusion II follows).

questions.stem:
A family consists of seven members: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V spanning three generations. There are two married couples.
• P is the paternal grandfather of V.
• Q is the only son of P.
• R is the daughter-in-law of P and mother of V.
• S is the sister of Q.
• T is the sister-in-law of R and is unmarried.
• U is the husband of S and father of a daughter.

How is Q related to V?
questions.explanation: P is grandfather of V, and Q is the only son of P. R is mother of V and wife of Q. Therefore, Q is the father of V.

questions.stem: How is S related to V?
questions.explanation: S is the sister of Q (V's father). Therefore, S is V's father's sister, which is Paternal Aunt (Bua).

questions.stem: How is U related to Q?
questions.explanation: U is the husband of S, who is Q's sister. Therefore, U is Q's sister's husband (Brother-in-law).

questions.stem: A cyclist starts from Point P, rides 12 km North to Point Q, turns East and rides 9 km to Point R. He then turns South and rides 12 km to Point S. In which direction and at what distance is Point S from Point P?
questions.explanation: Net North-South movement = 12 km North - 12 km South = 0 km. Net East movement = 9 km East. Hence Point S is exactly 9 km East of Point P.

In the following questions, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both the equations and mark the correct option:
Equation I: x² − 14x + 48 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0

In the following questions, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both the equations and mark the correct option:
Equation I: x² − 7x + 12 = 0
Equation II: y² − 13y + 40 = 0
questions.explanation:

questions.stem:
In the following questions, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both the equations and mark the correct option:
Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0 ⇒ (y − 6)(y − 7) = 0 ⇒ y = 6, 7.
Comparing roots:
• When x = 8: 8 > 6 and 8 > 7
• When x = 7: 7 > 6 and 7 = 7
Hence x ≥ y.

questions.stem:
In the following questions, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both the equations and mark the correct option:

For Eq II: y² − 14y + 48 = 0 ⇒ (y − 6)(y − 8) = 0 ⇒ y = 6, 8.
Comparing roots:
• When x = 4: 4 < 6 and 4 < 8
• When x = 6: 6 = 6 and 6 < 8
Hence x ≤ y.

questions.stem:
Find the missing number (?) in the given series:
12, 7, 9, 16.5, 37, ?

What will come in place of (?) in the following number series?
15, 16, 24, 51, 115, ?
questions.explanation:
The difference pattern is cubes of consecutive natural numbers:
• 16 − 15 = 1 (1³)
• 24 − 16 = 8 (2³)
• 51 − 24 = 27 (3³)
• 115 − 51 = 64 (4³)
• Next term = 115 + 5³ = 115 + 125 = 240.

questions.stem:
Find the next term in the series:
8, 14, 26, 44, 68, ?

Identify the missing term in the sequence:
5, 9, 16, 29, 54, ?

Find the WRONG number in the given series:
4, 11, 25, 53, 108, 221
questions.explanation:
The correct pattern is (n × 2 + 3):
• 4 × 2 + 3 = 11
• 11 × 2 + 3 = 25
• 25 × 2 + 3 = 53
• 53 × 2 + 3 = 109 (Instead of 108)
• 109 × 2 + 3 = 221
Therefore, 108 is the wrong number.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 25% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 125 : 100 = 5 : 4.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 4 × 30 = 120 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (5 + 4) × 6 = 54 units.
Remaining work = 120 − 54 = 66 units.
Time taken by A alone = 66 ÷ 5 = 13.2 days (say 14 approx or let's use exact numbers: B=30, efficiency A:B=5:4, work=120. If they work for 6 days, 54 units. Rem=66/5=13.2. Let's make efficiency 20% more: A:B=6:5, B takes 30 days -> Work = 150. Both 6 days = 11*6=66. Rem = 84/6 = 14 days!).
Exact days = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3:1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L → Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L → Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 4 : 3, and its perimeter is 112 meters. A circular garden has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular garden (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter = 2(l + b) = 112 ⇒ l + b = 56 m.
Ratio 4 : 3 ⇒ 7x = 56 ⇒ x = 8.
Length = 4 × 8 = 32 m, Breadth = 3 × 8 = 24 m (If r=14m: 2(14+b)).
Let l : b = 5 : 2, perimeter = 98 ⇒ 2(7x) = 98 ⇒ x = 7 ⇒ b = 14 m.
Area of circular garden = πr² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².
